title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## OpenTac: Open Ecosystem for Customizable 3D Tactile Sensing

### The Breakthrough
OpenTac introduces a resistive tactile skin plus a full‑stack design and simulation ecosystem that lets users generate custom 3‑D tactile sensors from outlines or text. Its structured deformable overlay converts tangential loads into spatial pressure, enabling neighboring taxels to infer shear while a common‑mode response captures normal force. A CAD‑driven tool automatically creates fabrication files, and an adaptive acquisition scheme runs at kilohertz rates, achieving 19.2× faster readouts than full‑array raster scanning on a 1024‑taxel skin. The authors validate more than 30 fabricated skins on four robot platforms for contact‑rich manipulation learning.

### The Caveats
The work provides no baseline comparison to existing tactile skins, so the claimed superiority and scalability remain unsubstantiated.

## DiffDreamer: World‑Model + Differentiable Simulation for Agile Quadrotor Control

### The Breakthrough
DiffDreamer couples a learned world model with a differentiable physics simulator, propagating external dynamics in latent space while the simulator updates the quadrotor's state in the same optimization step. The actor loss combines a critic‑driven term for non‑differentiable rewards and a simulator‑driven term for differentiable motion rewards. Experiments show faster convergence and higher final success rates than model‑free, model‑based, differentiable‑RL baselines and classical planners on aggressive tracking and gate‑racing benchmarks.

### The Caveats
Performance gains are demonstrated only in simulation and a single proof‑of‑concept flight, leaving real‑world robustness unverified.

## Humanoid Mobility via Attention‑Based Contacts

### The Breakthrough
The paper presents a self‑supervised attention‑based contact planner that predicts future foot contacts, feeding a contact‑conditioned tracker which generates coordinated whole‑body motions. This interface lets a single policy leverage motion‑data priors for naturalness while using reinforcement learning to explore environment‑dependent behaviors without reference inputs at deployment.

### The Caveats
No comparison to existing humanoid locomotion baselines is provided, so the claimed versatility remains unverified.

## Coordinated Multi‑Robot Path Planning via Root‑Locus Harmonic Functions

### The Breakthrough
By mapping a planar workspace to a circular domain, robot start and goal positions become poles and zeros of a rational function; the Generalized Root Locus of this function yields disjoint streamlines that guide each robot to its goal while guaranteeing obstacle avoidance via Milne‑Thomson reflections. A finite‑reflection test certifies safety and the gain acts as a clock so all robots arrive simultaneously, outperforming independent harmonic and artificial‑potential planners in simulated trials.

### The Caveats
The method is evaluated only in simulation on up to ten robots, with no real‑world experiments or larger‑team tests.

## RoboJev: 27B Open‑Source Model Grades Robot Videos 48× Cheaper, 28× Faster

### The Breakthrough
RoboJev fine‑tunes a 27‑billion‑parameter vision‑language model (JEV‑27B‑VL) with LoRA on 52,598 robot episodes and uses it as a reward model to score video streams in real‑time. Evaluating 68,555 episodes costs just $13.16 of GPU time, a 48× cost reduction and 28× speedup versus the proprietary 6 Astra model.

### The Caveats
The cheap, fast automated grading is untested on real robots and isn’t benchmarked against human labeling, as evaluation is limited to offline video datasets.

## Baidu Tests Robotaxi on London Streets

### The Breakthrough
Baidu is deploying its robotaxi stack for on‑road testing in London, marking one of the first evaluations of a Chinese autonomous‑driving system on European public streets.

### The Caveats
The announcement provides no performance, safety data, or comparisons to other autonomous‑driving systems, leaving its significance unverified.

## Free Course on Building a Claude Code‑Style Coding‑Agent Harness

### The Breakthrough
The creator shows that swapping only the harness around a fixed LLM can raise coding‑agent performance from 53% to 67% on the Terminal‑Bench benchmark, and provides an 8‑article, 6‑video open‑source course detailing harness design, sandboxing, context engineering, and deployment.

### The Caveats
The post offers no empirical evaluation or baseline comparison, so the reported gains and applicability to robotics remain unverified.

## nano‑ros: No‑Std Rust ROS 2 Client for Microcontrollers and RTOS

### The Breakthrough
nano‑ros implements a zero‑copy, no‑std ROS 2 middleware stack in Rust built on zenoh‑pico, supporting Zephyr, FreeRTOS, NuttX, ThreadX and Linux, with pluggable back‑ends (Zenoh, XRCE‑DDS, Cyclone DDS) and formal‑verification integration.

### The Caveats
The library offers only toy QEMU demos with minimal real‑hardware tests and no performance or latency comparison to existing micro‑ROS stacks.

## Calibrex: Command‑Line Sensor Calibration Check & Estimate for ROS Bags

### The Breakthrough
Calibrex batch‑optimizes sensor extrinsics from ROS 1/2 bags and reports per‑axis pass/fail metrics, reducing LiDAR‑LiDAR point‑to‑plane residuals from 19.1 cm to 4.4 cm and gyro‑deskew surface thickness from 3.42 cm to 2.19 cm on real datasets.

### The Caveats
It is evaluated only on offline bag datasets against vendor files and Kalibr, without comparison to newer calibration suites or real‑time tests.

### What to watch
Simulation‑driven control and planning papers (DiffDreamer, Humanoid Mobility, and the Root‑Locus path planner) each propose novel interfaces—differentiable physics, attention‑based contact prediction, and harmonic‑function streamlines—to bridge learned models and traditional robotics. Their differing emphases on agility, natural locomotion, and provable safety hint at complementary directions for next‑generation embodied AI.

### Priority
OpenTac delivers immediate, hardware‑level tactile sensing improvements together with a full design‑to‑deployment ecosystem, making it the most actionable breakthrough for robot developers today.

### One action
Download the OpenTac CAD files and fabricate a simple 3‑D tactile skin to equip your robot’s gripper for contact‑rich experiments.
